summary.text: The earthborn Giant who was immortal so long as he fought in the land of his birth, slain by Heracles when Athena advised the hero to drag him outside Pallene.

story.text: Apollodorus ranks Alcyoneus with Porphyrion as chief among the Giants whom Gaia bore in wrath over the Titans. He was immortal while he fought in his native land and had driven away the cows of the Sun from Erythia. Heracles first shot him with an arrow, but when the Giant fell he somewhat revived; at Athena's advice Heracles dragged him outside Pallene, and so he died. The Gigantomachy as a whole belongs to the Giants together; Alcyoneus is one of those Apollodorus names in its battle roll.
This Alcyoneus is not to be confused with Alcyone, the Pleiad daughter of Atlas and Pleione.
